title: Load, initialise and tell the class-loading failures apart

blocks.text: Class loading has three phases: **loading** finds the bytes and creates the `Class`, **linking** verifies and prepares it, and **initialization** runs the static initializers. The failures look alike but mean different things:

items: `ClassNotFoundException` (checked): a dynamic lookup such as `Class.forName` found no such class.
`ExceptionInInitializerError`: the class's static initializer threw, the first time the class was initialised.
`NoClassDefFoundError`: every later use of that class, which the JVM has marked unusable.

blocks.text: Write `ClassProbe` with the nested enum `Outcome { LOADED, NOT_FOUND, INIT_FAILED, UNUSABLE }`:

items: `initialise(name, loader)` loads **and initialises** the class through `loader` and returns the outcome; it never throws for these three failures.
`isPresent(name, loader)` says whether the class can be loaded, **without initialising it**.

rows: `isPresent(broken, loader)` on a fresh broken class
`true`, and its static block has not run

cases.says: initialise() loads and initialises String and a counted class (its static block runs once), and reports an unknown name as NOT_FOUND.
A class whose static initializer throws gives INIT_FAILED the first time and UNUSABLE every time after.
isPresent() finds a class without running its static initializer, even one whose initializer would throw.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: ClassNotFoundException is a checked failure of a dynamic lookup, while a failed static initializer gives ExceptionInInitializerError once and NoClassDefFoundError on every later use.
Loading, linking and initialization are separate phases, and a class can be loaded without running its static initializers.
